```text
# PR #4740: Patch: follow-up to #4706 from the after-merge spot-check

Closes #4720

## What changed

The test `r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions` (`crates/cards/src/patch_history.rs`) required every deck card in the working `catalog.json` to have play versions in `patches.json`. That fails on any pull request that adds a card to a shipped set or releases a set, because those cards reach `patches.json` only at the post-merge `patches ship`. Right now the 24 non-token Infinite Assault cards are left out only because `set_ships(InfiniteAssault)` is false, so the pull request that ships that set would have turned this test red.

The test now checks only the deck cards that the **newest shipped catalog** holds (`catalog_defs_at(CATALOG_VERSION)`). The other checks stay, for every card the history holds: unique ids, no `@`, `id == play_version_id(card, first)`, no gap in the versions, and exactly one live version (the last, ending at `catalog_version()`). The old count check, `by_card.len() == deckable`, is now stricter: the cards must match exactly and in catalog order.

- **`crates/cards/src/patch_history.rs`**
  - Two test helpers: `held_deck_cards` (deck cards of a catalog that the newest snapshot holds) and `assert_every_held_card_contiguous` (the old test body, taking the catalog and the newest snapshot as arguments).
  - The existing test is rewritten to call the helper on the real catalog.
  - New test `r4675000_a_deck_card_the_shipped_history_lacks_yet_has_no_play_versions`: it adds `core-999` (a copy of `core-001`) to a clone of the catalog. It checks that the new card has no play versions and is not counted, and that the full check still passes for that catalog.
  - The doc comment of `deck_play_versions` now says such a card has no play versions until `patches ship`. The function body is unchanged.
- **`crates/cards/README.md`** and **`spec/rulings/R4675000.md`**: the same one clause. No id, link or `proven_in` changes. `spec/pending/4675.md` does not repeat this text, so the daily fold has nothing to reconcile.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean after `cargo fmt -p jackioh-cards`, which split one `assert!` over several lines.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --lib patch_history`: 9 passed, 0 failed, including both R4675000 tests above.
- **Check that the new test catches the old behaviour:** I removed `&& newest.contains_key(&def.id)` from `held_deck_cards` and ran `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --lib r4675000`. The new test failed at `patch_history.rs:502`, the `!held.contains(&"core-999")` assert, and the other 5 passed. I then restored the file and confirmed the diff was back to what it was.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`: `10361 passed; 0 failed` and `1248 passed; 0 failed`.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-cards --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: `2451 rulings, 6124 proofs, 75582 citations in 4721 files, 33684 links: ok`.
- `cargo jackioh catalog check` and `cargo jackioh patches check`: ok. The catalog census still lists Infinite Assault as not shipped (24 cards + 2 tokens).
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: `classify: Internal`.
- **Not run locally:** the workspace-wide `cargo test` and `clippy`, and the web tests. Only the cards crate's tests changed, nothing outside it reads them, and no `ts`-exported type changed. The harness runs the full suites.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **Which cards the history holds is read from the newest shipped snapshot.**
  - Rejected: catalog cards with an `added` line in `patches.json`. That is circular, because those are the change lines under test.
  - Rejected: skipping the cards a pending fragment adds. The fragments are not compiled into `jackioh-cards`, the crate's purity rule (CLAUDE.md rule 4) bars reading them from disk in tests, and a set's release need not list each card in a fragment.
  - The snapshot is independent of the change lines: `history.rs`'s `build()` rebuilds it from `patches/<newest>.json` using the `absent` ids that `build.rs` writes.
- **`deck_play_versions` keeps its behaviour.** It already gives such a card no versions (`unwrap_or_default`). Rejected: making it panic or report the missing card, which would break the same workflow on the server and in `cargo jackioh stats`.
- **No new ruling.** No game rule changes; the change makes R4675000's note clearer.
- I followed the plan step by step with no departures.

## Worth a second look

- The new test passes its synthetic `branch` catalog to the helper, but `deck_play_versions()` still reads the real `CATALOG`. That is what a branch would see: its new card is in the catalog and absent from `patches.json`. Making `deck_play_versions` take a catalog would mean changing its body, which the plan ruled out.
- A card the snapshot holds but `patches.json` drops still fails the test, because of the exact match in catalog order.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `claude-4`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 10 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.
```

````text
# #4720: Patch: follow-up to #4706 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #4706 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #4706 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45382603995)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`863732844756`). `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #4706 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `crates/cards/src/patch_history.rs:449`: The test `r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions` requires every deckable card in the working `catalog.json` to have play versions in `patches.json`. That breaks the repository's normal card workflow: a new card, or a whole set's cards when the set ships, reach `catalog.json` in the PR but reach `patches.json` only at the post-merge `patches ship`. So this test fails on every PR that adds a non-token card to a shipped set or releases a set, and on `main` between that merge and the ship.
  Evidence: The test computes `deckable` from `crate::CATALOG` (the parsed working `catalog.json`, lib.rs:117) filtered by `!def.token && set_ships(def.set)`, and asserts `by_card.len() == deckable`, where `by_card` comes from `deck_play_versions()`, which reads only `patches.json`. A card missing from `patches.json` becomes an empty list (`unwrap_or_default`), so `by_card.len()` is smaller than `deckable`. `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md:32` says `catalog.json` and `patches.json` themselves 'need no edit for a new card'. Lines 195-221 say the history moves only at the post-merge promotion (`patches-ship.yml`). Precedent: the Stinkyscape+ release, cefa23e20e (#3786), changed `catalog.json` (+8698 lines) and `catalog_types.rs` (the set ships) with no `patches.json` change; its cards entered the history only in the later ship commit e439669a48 (#3830). With this test in place, that PR would have been red. The held Infinite Assault set (tracker #4576) will hit this when it ships. Fix: count only the cards the shipped history holds (for example, catalog cards that appear in the newest snapshot or in an `added` line), or skip catalog cards that a pending fragment adds, while keeping the contiguity and one-live checks for every card that is in the history.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

---

## Goal

`r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions` in `crates/cards/src/patch_history.rs` must stop requiring every deck card in the working `catalog.json` to have play versions in `patches.json`. A card that a branch adds, or one of a set that a branch releases, reaches `catalog.json` in its pull request but reaches the history only at the post-merge `patches ship` (`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md`, rows 9 and 30–33). After the fix the test checks exactly the deck cards that the **newest shipped catalog** holds. It keeps the checks on ids, contiguity and the one live version for each of those cards. A new test shows that a deck card on a branch which the history lacks is no longer counted. `deck_play_versions()`'s behaviour does not change. Its doc comment, `crates/cards/README.md` and the R4675000 note now say that such a card has no play versions until the ship.

Evidence this is real: today `catalog.json` holds 1,005 entries and the newest snapshot (`crates/cards/patches/v0.6.12d.json`) holds 979. The 26 missing are Infinite Assault cards (24 non-token). The only thing filtering them out is `set_ships(InfiniteAssault) == false`, so the PR that ships that set would turn this test red.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/cards/src/patch_history.rs` | change | Doc comment of `deck_play_versions`. In `mod tests`: `use jackioh_engine::CardDefs`, new helpers `held_deck_cards` and `assert_every_held_card_contiguous`, the body of `r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions` rewritten, and a new test `r4675000_a_deck_card_the_shipped_history_lacks_yet_has_no_play_versions` |
| `crates/cards/README.md` | change | The `deck_play_versions()` sentence in the `play_versions()` bullet (around line 390) |
| `spec/rulings/R4675000.md` | change | One clause added to the first paragraph's `deck_play_versions` sentence |

Do not touch: `spec/pending/4675.md`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md` (the daily fold owns them), `crates/cards/patches/**`, `crates/cards/catalog.json`, any other crate or app, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`. No pending patch fragment: no card's data or play changes.

Governing spec: R4675000 (play versions; `deck_play_versions`), R1367000 (reading `patches.json`), R767000 / R388 (the shipped snapshots that `catalog_defs_at` rebuilds), R646 (pending-claimed cards), R1420 (`set_ships`). **No new ruling**: no game rule changes, and the test's reading follows from R4675000 plus the ship workflow, so nothing goes in issue #4720's block (R4720000+).

## Steps

1. **`crates/cards/src/patch_history.rs`, doc comment of `pub fn deck_play_versions`** (lines 232–233). Replace the two `///` lines with:
   ```rust
   /// R4675000: the play versions of every card a deck can hold, in catalog order: the catalog's cards that
   /// are no token, of a set that ships (R1420), each card's oldest first. A card `catalog.json` holds before
   /// the shipped history does, one a branch adds or of a set a branch releases, has none until
   /// `patches ship` writes it into `patches.json` (docs/ADDING_CARDS.md).
   ```
   Do not change the function body.

2. **Same file, `mod tests` imports** (line 245, after `use super::*;`): add `use jackioh_engine::CardDefs;`.

3. **Same file, new test helper `held_deck_cards`**. Put it directly above the test `r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions`:
   ```rust
   /// R4675000: the deck cards the shipped history holds, in `catalog`'s order: its cards that are no
   /// token, of a set that ships, and that `newest`, the newest shipped catalog, holds. A card a branch
   /// adds, or one of a set a branch releases, reaches `catalog.json` in its pull request and the history
   /// only at `patches ship`.
   fn held_deck_cards<'a>(catalog: &'a CardDefs, newest: &CardDefs) -> Vec<&'a str> {
       catalog
           .values()
           .filter(|def| !def.token && jackioh_engine::set_ships(def.set) && newest.contains_key(&def.id))
           .map(|def| def.id.as_str())
           .collect()
   }
   ```

4. **Same file, new helper `assert_every_held_card_contiguous`**. Put it right after `held_deck_cards`. Move the current test body into it, with one change: the `deckable` count and `assert_eq!(by_card.len(), deckable);` (lines 445–449) are replaced by a check that the card ids match exactly and in catalog order. Copy every other line from the current body unchanged:

   /// R4675000: `versions` hold exactly the deck cards of `catalog` that `newest` holds, in catalog order,
   /// each over the shipped versions from where it was added to the newest without a gap, its newest
   /// play version alone live.
   fn assert_every_held_card_contiguous(versions: &[PlayVersion], catalog: &CardDefs, newest: &CardDefs) {
       let shipped = crate::shipped_versions();
       let mut ids: IndexSet<&str> = IndexSet::new();
       let mut by_card: IndexMap<&str, Vec<&PlayVersion>> = IndexMap::new();
       for version in versions {
           assert!(ids.insert(&version.id), "{} repeats", version.id);
           assert!(!version.id.contains('@'), "{}", version.id);
           assert_eq!(version.id, play_version_id(&version.card, version.first()));
           by_card.entry(&version.card).or_default().push(version);
       }
       let held = held_deck_cards(catalog, newest);
       assert!(!held.is_empty(), "the newest shipped catalog holds deck cards");
       assert_eq!(by_card.keys().copied().collect::<Vec<&str>>(), held);
       for (card, versions) in &by_card {
           // … lines 451–463 of the current test, verbatim …
       }
   }
   ```
   The loop body is the current one: `spanned`, `from`, `assert_eq!(spanned, shipped[from..], "{card}")`, the `live` vector and its three assertions.

5. **Same file, rewrite the body of `r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions`**. Keep the name and `#[test]`:
   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions() {
       let newest = crate::catalog_defs_at(crate::CATALOG_VERSION).expect("the newest is carried");
       assert_every_held_card_contiguous(&deck_play_versions(), &crate::CATALOG, newest);
   }
   ```
   (`&crate::CATALOG` deref-coerces from `&LazyLock<CardDefs>`. `catalog_defs_at` needs no `register_all`, as `history.rs`'s `r388_catalog_defs_at_rebuilds_every_shipped_snapshot_exact` shows.)

6. **Same file, new test right after it**, `r4675000_a_deck_card_the_shipped_history_lacks_yet_has_no_play_versions`:
   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn r4675000_a_deck_card_the_shipped_history_lacks_yet_has_no_play_versions() {
       let newest = crate::catalog_defs_at(crate::CATALOG_VERSION).expect("the newest is carried");
       // A branch adds a Core card: `catalog.json` holds it in the pull request, `patches.json` only after
       // `patches ship`.
       let mut branch = crate::CATALOG.clone();
       let mut added = crate::card_def("core-001");
       added.id = "core-999".to_string();
       assert!(branch.insert(added.id.clone(), added).is_none(), "core-999 is no catalog card yet");
       assert!(!newest.contains_key("core-999"));
       assert!(!play_versions().contains_key("core-999"));
       let held = held_deck_cards(&branch, newest);
       assert!(!held.contains(&"core-999"));
       assert!(held.contains(&"core-001"));
       // The branch's deck cards are the shipped ones and its own: the new card has none, and every card
       // the history holds still has contiguous versions.
       assert_every_held_card_contiguous(&deck_play_versions(), &branch, newest);
   }

7. **`crates/cards/README.md`**, the `play_versions()` bullet (around lines 390–391). Replace
   `` `deck_play_versions()` keeps a deck's cards, which the engine's `play_version_figures` reads (`GET /api/stats/versions`, R4675001). ``
   with
   `` `deck_play_versions()` keeps a deck's cards, which the engine's `play_version_figures` reads (`GET /api/stats/versions`, R4675001); a card `catalog.json` holds before the history does, one a branch adds or of a set a branch releases, has none until `patches ship`. ``

   `` `deck_play_versions` keeps the cards a deck can hold, those of a set that ships and no token, in catalog order; a card `catalog.json` holds before the history does, one a branch adds or of a set a branch releases, has none until `patches ship` writes its `added` line. ``
   Leave the front matter and every other sentence alone.

- `r4675000_the_compiled_in_history_gives_every_shipped_card_contiguous_versions`: the deck cards that `deck_play_versions()` covers are exactly, and in catalog order, the deck cards of `CATALOG` that the newest shipped catalog holds. Each play version id is unique, has no `@` and equals `play_version_id(card, first)`. Each card spans the shipped versions without a gap from its first to the newest, with exactly one live version, the last, ending at `catalog_version()`.
- `r4675000_a_deck_card_the_shipped_history_lacks_yet_has_no_play_versions` (new): `core-999` (a copy of `core-001`) added to a clone of the catalog is not held, has no play versions, and the full check still passes for that catalog.
````
